claim.why_it_matters: The single meta-language term table is split into two tables, a stray <pre> block holding the wrapped tail 'table-format)' of the occurs-clause row, and two rows (validate-status-clause, value-clause) demoted to loose paragraph text; the occurs-clause cell is truncated mid-word inside its row. All words survive, but a reader or tool parsing the table loses the occurs-clause format list and the last two term-to-subclause mappings.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (ISO/IEC 1989:2014 p.289, PDF p.313) shows one borderless two-column Term/Subclause list of nine rows; the occurs-clause subclause text wraps in the PDF itself at 'dynamic-capacity-' / 'table-format)'. The markdown carries every term and every subclause mapping word for word in the same order: the occurs-clause row plus its wrapped tail 'table-format)' in the following <pre>, picture/select-when/usage in a second table, and 'validate-status-clause 13.18.62, VALIDATE-STATUS clause' and 'value-clause 13.18.63, VALUE clause (data-item or table format)' as paragraph lines. The claim describes the markup fragmentation accurately, but nothing is missing, misquoted or altered: the split follows the PDF's own line wrap and the difference is purely table formatting with no change in meaning. Rejected as a formatting-only difference.
